text:
maria: heads-up — rolled AWQ int8 onto canary for chat-prod yesterday. unit perf looks good but we see accuracy delta on the safety evals and weird latency spikes when prefix cache is warm.

maria: quick summary:
- avg latency down 18% when cold, p95 improved too
- safety F1 dropped ~2.4% on the 3k safety prompts compared to fp16 baseline
- intermittently see p99 spikes ~2–3x only when prefix-cache hit rate > 70% and batch size estimator goes above 8

maria: repro snippet of the logs when spike happens:
```
[2026-07-12T14:22:11Z] batcher: estimate_batch_size -> 12 (seq_dist skewed)
[2026-07-12T14:22:11Z] cache: prefix_hit rate=0.78 keys=1412
[2026-07-12T14:22:11Z] runtime: awq-kernel select -> int8-awq-fast
[2026-07-12T14:22:11Z] runtime: kvcache-miss -> fallback to decoding loop (slow path)
[2026-07-12T14:22:11Z] latency: request 0x7f -> 412ms (p99)
```

alex: interesting. sounds like quant-induced path variance + cache interaction. when int8 kernel chooses a fast path, we might be shuffling between cached KV layouts and the runtime ends up serializing some work.

ryan: do we have a counterexample where cache hit rate high but no spike? or is it deterministic with certain sequence lengths?

maria: not deterministic — correlated with skewed sequence-length distribution (lots of short prefixes + occasional long continuations). continuous-batcher upsizes batch based on recent samples, then a long continuation forces a slow path and stalls the whole batch.

nora: could be that AWQ's attention matmul uses a different scratch layout that isn't compatible with cached key-value encoding, so runtime does a convert on the hot path. conversion cost + big batch -> p99.

bench-bot: metrics snapshot:
- workload: chat-prod-canary
- model: gptx-30b-awq-int8
- baseline: gptx-30b-fp16
- token/sec: +12%
- avg latency: 142ms -> 116ms
- p95: 312ms -> 262ms
- p99 (spiky): 410ms -> 940ms (on spike events)
- safety-f1: 0.912 -> 0.892

alex: hypothesis list:
1) runtime chooses awq-int8 kernel that requires converting cached KV blocks -> conversion cost in slow path
2) batch estimator overshoots during prefix-heavy traffic causing larger synchronization stalls
3) quantization reduces numeric margin leading to small safety regressions on edge prompts

ryan: propose quick experiments (A/B) on canary:
- A: disable prefix cache for awq-int8 (route to no-prefetch) — measure p99 and token/sec
- B: cap batcher max_batch_size to 8 for awq-int8 deployments
- C: run the safety eval with higher-precision fallback enabled for safety-critical prompts (runtime rule)

maria: logging plan: add a tag on each request indicating kernel + cache-compat flag and record conversion_time per request. also dump a small sample of prompts that flipped safety label.

nora: I'll look at kernel source to see if we can make KV format zero-copy compatible or at least async-convert off the critical path.

alex: timeline: run A/B overnight on 5% of canary traffic, collect 24h metrics. if p99 improves and safety drop persists, enable C for safety prompts and run regression harness on 10k eval set.

maria: quick command to flip prefix cache for awq-int8 on canary route:
```
# run from infra tools
redwood route update --route chat-prod-canary --model gptx-30b-awq-int8 --prefix-cache false --commit
```

ryan: I'll set up the batcher cap experiment and the eval job. tagging @nora for kernel follow-up.

nora: ack. will post kernel notes here once I confirm layout details.

maria: thanks team — will post the 24h summary tomorrow. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
